text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Lennart Meri was sworn in for his new term in the parliament.
- The government and the public sector trade union TALO signed an agreement for 14 percent pay rise in 1997.
- Estonian politicians have to decide soon whether to continue to insist on the recognition of Tartu Peace Treaty by Russia or give up the demand, Foreign Minister Siim Kallas told the parliament.
- Russia deputy Foreign Minister in September warned the Estonian Ambassador Mart Helme that negotiations over Chechnya's recognition would result in Russia's severing diplomatic relations.
- The number of crimes in the first eight months of 1996 dropped 11 percent compared with the same period in 1995. The number of crimes solved has risen by five percent.
- The decision of the government not to grant Estonian citizenship to businessman Mark Rivkin and his family was legal, the Tallinn Administrative Court ruled.
- Eesti Telefon will invest 300 million kroons in the next three years for developing communications in rural areas.
